subject: EdgeHealth pilot - request for warm-standby GPU carveout and SLA
messages:
From: Procurement Team <procurement@edgehealth.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: CTO, EdgeHealth <cto@edgehealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot standby capacity ask - HIPAA pilot (EdgeHealth)

Hi Markus,

We're getting close to kickoff for our HIPAA pilot (internal kickoff: 2026-11-08). To meet our SLA commitments with the hospital partner we need a 'warm-standby' reserved lane — capacity that's reserved and can scale to peak in under 3 minutes.

Can Redwood support a small dedicated standby pool (NVIDIA A100-equivalent, ~1.5k token/s sustained for concurrent 6 sessions) for the pilot window (Nov 8 — Dec 8)? We expect baseline usage to be low but need guaranteed headroom during peak processing.

Attached: a short SOW and a simple capacity spreadsheet. Also open to discussing a billing construct where standby is charged at a lower base + overage for active tokens.

Thanks,
Maya R. (procurement)
EdgeHealth
Attachments: EdgeHealth_MA_Pilot_SOW.pdf, capacity_estimate_edgehealth.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot standby capacity ask - HIPAA pilot (EdgeHealth)

Maya — thanks for the SOW and the clear ask. Looping in Kim (Product) and Laura (Capacity ops) to validate feasibility and propose a concrete runbook and pricing model.

Kim / Laura — quick context: EdgeHealth (EH-2026-PILOT-47) wants a warm-standby carveout for a 1-month HIPAA pilot. Target cold->peak latency for spin-up is <= 3 minutes. They propose a hybrid billing model (lower base + overage for active tokens). They flagged HIPAA compliance needs in the SOW.

Next steps I'd like:
- Laura: can we provision a small reserved slice with autoscale exception and define the fallback behavior if capacity is constrained?
- Kim: can you confirm product constraints (KV cache persistence, prefix caching windows) that affect 'warm' vs 'hot'?
- Finance sign-off required for a carveout discount if we accept standby billing.

I'll coordinate timeline after your recommendations.

—Markus
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot standby capacity ask - HIPAA pilot (EdgeHealth)

Thanks for looping me in. High level: product can support the pattern but there are trade-offs we should call out for the customer and Ops.

Notes:
- Warm-standby definition: we can keep model weights and a small KV cache resident to reduce cold-starts, but full-hot (zero cold penalty) requires continuous minimal traffic or a higher reserved memory footprint.
- Cache TTL: recommend 24-hour prefix cache retention for the pilot to balance cost and responsiveness; this is configurable but affects memory footprint.
- Autoscale exception: ops will need a temporary policy that raises max-burst and reduces cooldowns; that can be enabled for the pilot window but it requires manual rollback or a scheduled revert.

Questions for the customer:
1) Do you need persistent KV cache across restarts (for session continuity), or is session rehydrate acceptable?
2) Can you commit to a minimal heartbeat (e.g., 1 req / 10min) during off-peak to keep the slice warmer at lower cost?

I'll draft suggested config options (cache TTL, heartbeat model, failover to compatible quantized variant) once answers above are in.

—Kim
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot standby capacity ask - HIPAA pilot (EdgeHealth)

Adding ops detail and a proposed runbook.

Runbook (high level):
1) Provisioning: create a dedicated pool slice (2 x A100-equivalent slots) reserved Nov 6 (48h pre-warm) — label EH-PILOT-47-standby.
2) Warm strategy: keep model diags loaded, allocate reduced KV cache (configurable; default 24h TTL), and enable a low-cost keepalive job (customer heartbeat or Redwood synthetic ping).
3) Autoscale exception: temporary policy to allow burst to 6 concurrent sessions, with pre-defined throttles and a soft-fallback to a quantized variant after 3 minutes if resources exhausted.
4) Monitoring + alerts: create dedicated dashboards and a paging rule to on-call if error-rate > 1% during peak windows.
5) Rollback: schedule automatic rollback of the policy on Dec 9 at 02:00 UTC and a teardown job Dec 12 unless extended by contract amendment.

Operational caveats:
- This will reduce flexible pool capacity during the window — potential exposure if multiple enterprise pilots overlap. We need a pre-approval from finance for the carveout discount to consider the reservation economically sensible.
- For HIPAA, we'll use the Private deployment control plane with customer-approved routing; legal/infosec needs to confirm no additional controls are needed.

I'll prepare a short ops agreement and a proposed SLA (uptime target, spin-up SLO) for the customer to review.

—Laura
Senior Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot standby capacity ask - HIPAA pilot (EdgeHealth)

Thanks — finance perspective below.

We can greenlight a limited carveout for a 1-month pilot under these constraints:
- Billing construct: 50% of reserved pool monthly rate + usage overage billed per-token beyond a 10M token threshold.
- Discount authorization: up to 30% off standard reserved pricing for pilots under 3 months (requires revenue ops ticket).
- Contract language: must include a minimum notice for extension (14 days) and an explicit termination date.

Please add a line item in the SOW for the billing model and I'll kick off the revenue ops flow once the SOW includes the pricing table.

—Neha
Finance, Redwood Inference

Best,
Markus
